reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept {CONTROL IS | CONTROLS ARE} followed by either {data-name-1}... or FINAL [data-name-1]... (FINAL once and first; data-name-1 possibly qualified but, per the 1985 definition of data-name, never subscripted or reference-modified), and build the hierarchy FINAL > first data-name > ... > last data-name.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.SubscriptedClauseOperands (Year == 2002): a subscripted operand is admitted only at 2002
construct report-control-reference-modification-2002: a ref-modified control operand refused below 2002
DialectLevel >= 2002: written-reference uniqueness (2023 SR6); at 85 ScreenControlItemsDistinct asks the 1985 SR2 resolved-item test instead

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: reference modification of data-name-1 is refused at 85 (COBOL0900) and admitted from 2002; an index data item is admitted at 85; 85 tests distinct items, 2002+ distinct written references
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover FINAL-first and an index data item; CONTROLS ARE with qualified operands, the refusal of FINAL after a data-name or twice, the subscripted and ref-modified operands and the wrong IS/ARE pairing are not exercised

probes.printed: report: AAAA 11 / AAAA 11 / CF-Y / AAAA 22 / CF-Y / CF-X / BBAA 22 / CF-Y / CF-X / CF-F
probes.expected: CONTROLS ARE FINAL CX OF GRP CY: minor break on CY gives CF-Y, major break on CX gives CF-Y then CF-X, TERMINATE gives CF-Y, CF-X, CF-F
CONTROL CX IN GRP CY (no FINAL) accepted, same hierarchy

probes.printed: COBOL2421 FINAL is written after the data-name 'CX OF GRP'
COBOL2421 FINAL is written more than once

probes.expected: refused: data-name may not be subscripted (§1985:III.2)

probes.printed: COBOL0900 a reference-modified control name requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused: data-name may not be reference-modified (§1985:III.2)
refused: CONTROL pairs with IS only
refused: CONTROLS pairs with ARE only

probes.printed: COBOL1699 ... must identify a different data item (ISO §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR2)

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.2  (3.7.2 General Format)  the text is in the clause [quote: CONTROLS ARE FINAL data-name-1]
OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.4 GR1  (3.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1
OK  §1985:III.2  (2. DEFINITIONS)  the text is in the clause [quote: must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted]

reader.notes: The grammar admits (FINAL | dataReference)+ and the binder refuses FINAL out of place (COBOL2421); the 1985 data-name definition is honoured by the subscript refusal and the version pass's ref-mod gate. Several messages cite 2023 clause numbers at --std 85, but each refusal is the one the 1985 text requires.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: cc1 CONTROLS FINAL, GRP, WN, WI (ARE omitted, a group, a signed scaled numeric and an index data item, comma separators) accepted, report AAAA 11 / AAAA 22 / CF-F; cc2 CONTROL FINAL (IS omitted) accepted, same. Refusals: cb1 CONTROL IS with no operand (COBOL0001), cb2 literal operand (COBOL5506), cb3 condition-name (COBOL0899 does not resolve to a data item), cb4 report-name, cb5 LINE-COUNTER, cb6 file-name (COBOL0899 each), cb7 FINAL after a data-name and repeated (COBOL2421), cb8 the clause written twice (COBOL2423). The reader's probes already covered subscript, ref-mod, IS/ARE pairing. The messages cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85 (text blemish, same as the reader noted). cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.7.2 [CONTROLS ARE FINAL data-name-1]; OK §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR1 [Data-name-1 may be qualified].
